title: Operational Audit Fidelity and Export Playbook with Northshore Analytics
next_steps: Maya to share SOC 2 type II report and latest pen-test summary
Connor to pull sample audit log export and redaction demo artifacts
Customer to provide list of regulatory regions and retention SLA targets
action_items: Owner: Maya Patel; Item: Share SOC2 report + security whitepaper; Due: 2026-01-02
Owner: Connor Li; Item: Prepare S3 export demo + Kafka webhook sample; Due: 2026-01-05
Owner: Samir Khan; Item: Provide list of event types required for compliance (fields & retention); Due: 2026-01-03
summary: Customer wanted to validate what admin and audit events Redwood captures, export destinations (S3/Kafka/BigQuery), retention/archival options, and KMS integration for key management. Redwood team explained default retention, streaming and batch export mechanisms, field-level redaction, and private deployment options for data residency. Agreed next steps: share SOC2 reports, run an export/redaction demo, and confirm retention policy for regulated regions.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. we scheduled an hour but we have a little buffer so feel free to air any deep technical reqs.
[00:00:08] Aisha Rahman: Great, thanks. We're specifically focused on admin activity capture — what is captured, how we can export it, and what controls we have for retention and encryption. also SOC2 stuff.
[00:00:20] Connor Li: Hey, quick intro — I'm Connor, I'm the solutions engineer on the account. we'll run through the event taxonomy and then demo an export flow.
[00:00:27] Tom Becker: Sorry, can you confirm this recording is ok? legal's ok with it for notes.
[00:00:30] Maya Patel: Yep noted, thanks.
[00:00:35] [00:00:35] Lena Ortiz: we got auditors next quarter so we need clear exportable trails.
[00:00:40] Connor Li: high level — our audit stream captures admin events (login, sso auth attempts, api key creation, api key deletion, role changes, permission grants/revokes, model deploys, rollout events, config changes, billing access, and data export operations). it also captures system-level telemetry like failed auths, ip address, user-agent, and action payloads.
[00:01:05] Samir Khan: payloads — are they full request bodies? we need to avoid storing PII in logs for GDPR.
[00:01:12] Connor Li: good question, we don't store sensitive document content by default. there are two layers: first, request metadata (who/when/what) is captured; second, payloads that might contain user data are redacted unless you've opted in to full payload retention. we also offer field-level redaction rules and automatic PII scrubbing for common patterns.
[00:01:35] Aisha Rahman: and what about encryption at rest — can we bring our own keys?
[00:01:40] Maya Patel: yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or an HSM integration). for hosted accounts we offer envelope encryption and a managed KMS, but we can do BYOK for Dedicated/Private with contractual terms.
[00:01:58] [00:01:58] Tom Becker: residency — we need logs to stay in eu-west for EU customers. how do you route exports by region?
[00:02:05] Connor Li: exports are region-aware. you can pin export destinations to a region (for example an eu-west S3 bucket), or run a Private control plane in the EU to avoid cross-border movement. we also provide the option to stream events to customer-owned Kafka in-region.
[00:02:25] Lena Ortiz: retention defaults? auditors want 7 years for some records — is that supported?
[00:02:30] Connor Li: default retention for admin events in hosted is 90 days, but we have archival options: automatic exports to S3 or BigQuery for long-term retention, and you can configure lifecycle rules on your bucket to keep data for 7 years. for Dedicated/Private customers we can store longer on-prem, depends on contract and storage sizing.
[00:02:52] [00:02:52] Aisha Rahman: how granular is the export? can we filter by event type, user, time range?
[00:02:57] Connor Li: yes — the export API and the console export UI let you filter by event_type, user_id, resource_id, time window, and tenant_id. for streaming we've got topic partitioning by tenant so you can subscribe to exactly the event stream you need.
[00:03:15] Samir Khan: do we get cryptographic hashes to prove immutability for audits?
[00:03:19] Connor Li: we can include an event-level SHA256 digest in the export bundle and sign batches. for high-integrity requirements we support append-only write modes to customer-owned storage with signed manifests. not quite blockchain but it's good for audit evidence.
[00:03:36] [00:03:36] Aisha Rahman: okay, SOC2 — do you provide the full report?
[00:03:40] Maya Patel: we can share our SOC 2 type II report and executive summary under an NDA if needed; we'll attach it to the thread. 
[00:03:48] Lena Ortiz: any known gaps in ISO or SOC we should know before auditors dig in?
[00:03:52] Maya Patel: nothing substantive for customers; we'll include the control scope and the auditor letter. should be fine but if you need a control mapping (redwood controls to ISO/SOC controls) we can provide that too.
[00:04:05] [00:04:05] Tom Becker: about API key lifecycle — what events are logged when a key is rotated and when it's used?
[00:04:11] Connor Li: we log key creation, rotation, deletion, and each usage is an event containing the key_id abstracted (we never log the raw key material). usage events include timestamp, request id, rate-limiting hits, and response codes.
[00:04:30] Samir Khan: and can we revoke retroactively — revoke and then scrub tokens from caches?
[00:04:34] Connor Li: yes, we have a token revocation endpoint and the serving runtime propagates revocation signals to edge nodes; there may be a short TTL for cached tokens but it's typically seconds. we can coordinate an immediate cache flush for Dedicated/private installs.
[00:04:51] [00:04:51] Aisha Rahman: show me the export paths — you mentioned S3 and Kafka and BigQuery — any others?
[00:04:58] Connor Li: supported sinks today: S3 (any region), GCS, BigQuery export connector, Azure Blob (preview), streaming to customer Kafka or Kinesis, and webhook delivery for event-forwarding. we also have a scheduled batch export that writes newline-delimited JSON to your bucket.
[00:05:18] Tom Becker: webhooks — guaranteed delivery? do you support retries and dead-letter queues?
[00:05:23] Connor Li: we have an at-least-once delivery model for webhooks with exponential backoff and configurable retry policy and a dead-letter topic you can inspect. for mission-critical ingest we recommend streaming to customer-owned Kafka.
[00:05:38] [00:05:38] Lena Ortiz: redaction — can you show examples of field-level redaction?
[00:05:42] Connor Li: sure — we apply regex-based rules and named field redaction. example: if an event contains a field named email or social_security_number, we replace values with a token like <REDACTED_EMAIL>. you can define custom rules and test them in the console.
[00:06:00] Samir Khan: do redactions occur before the export or after?
[00:06:03] Connor Li: redactions happen at the pipeline ingress — before data lands in any long-term export. we can also provide dual-mode: raw+redacted for customers that need to retain original payloads in a locked bucket with stricter access controls.
[00:06:18] [00:06:18] Aisha Rahman: is masking deterministic? meaning if I search across logs can I still link the same user without revealing PII?
[00:06:24] Connor Li: we support deterministic hashing (salted HMAC) for certain fields so you can link events without revealing the underlying value. salts are customer-controlled in BYOK flows.
[00:06:36] Tom Becker: what's the schema for events — is there a published schema we can validate against?
[00:06:40] Connor Li: yes, we publish the event schema and a JSON Schema file in the developer docs. columns include event_type, timestamp, tenant_id, user_id (hashed if requested), resource_id, ip_addr, user_agent, outcome, and an optional payload field with redacted content.
[00:06:58] [00:06:58] Lena Ortiz: can we onboard custom event types? like whenever our orchestration triggers a specific hook?
[00:07:03] Connor Li: you can emit custom audit events via the Audit API. they'll be treated like native events and can be forwarded to your sink.
[00:07:10] [00:07:10] Maya Patel: I want to call out compliance with access controls — RBAC mapping supports SSO groups and SCIM provisioning, we can sync group membership to roles in Redwood.
[00:07:21] Aisha Rahman: SAML/SSO — does the IdP assertion appear in logs?
[00:07:25] Connor Li: we log successful and failed SAML assertions metadata (issuer, subject, timestamp) but not the raw assertion by default. you can elect to store the assertion if you have strong reasons, but it's discouraged.
[00:07:39] [00:07:39] Samir Khan: for on-prem control plane — does the audit stream run locally or is there any telemetry that goes back to Redwood?
[00:07:46] Maya Patel: with Private deployments the control plane is customer-managed; audit logs can be kept entirely on-prem and we don't ship telemetry off-site unless you enable support and remote diagnostics.
[00:07:58] Tom Becker: okay, about ingestion scale — we expect millions of events per day. how do you handle throughput to S3/Kafka?
[00:08:06] Connor Li: we support high-throughput streaming with batching and back-pressure. for Kafka we write keyed partitions per tenant; for S3 we buffer small files and rotate to larger multi-GB objects for efficiency. we also provide put-object parallelism guidance for large ingest.
[00:08:24] [00:08:24] Lena Ortiz: time sync and clock drift — stamps must be trustworthy for audits.
[00:08:29] Connor Li: events are timestamped at ingestion with NTP-synced clocks and we attach a server_received_time in addition to client_ts so you have both perspectives.
[00:08:41] Maya Patel: quick interruption — a few typical customer tradeoffs: if you keep full payloads the storage and egress costs increase; redaction reduces forensic fidelity but helps minimize PII exposure. wanted to call that out because auditors often ask about these tradeoffs.
[00:08:56] [00:08:56] Aisha Rahman: makes sense. for our audit scope we need model-deploy events and content access events retained for 5 years and accessible to auditors. can that be surfaced?
[00:09:06] Connor Li: yes, we can configure the export to include model lifecycle events and operator-level content access for the retention window you require. if you need content access events containing snippets, we'd handle that via a locked, encrypted bucket with access controls and strict key management.
[00:09:24] Tom Becker: what about cost estimates for 5 years of events at ~100k events/day?
[00:09:29] Connor Li: we can provide a sizing worksheet; rough ballpark — storage is mostly S3/BigQuery cost; you'll want lifecycle tiering to Glacier/Coldline to be economical. we'll deliver a cost model in the follow-up.
[00:09:44] [00:09:44] Samir Khan: one more developer question — can we replay events into our SIEM?
[00:09:49] Connor Li: yes, exports can be replayed; we maintain sequence numbers and ordering metadata so you can rehydrate downstream systems.
[00:09:58] Lena Ortiz: is there a playground we can use to test redaction rules?
[00:10:02] Connor Li: in the console you can run test payloads against your redaction policy; we'll also bundle a sample CLI tool for batch testing.
[00:10:11] [00:10:11] Aisha Rahman: ok let's talk forensic readiness — if we have an incident will you provide raw logs for investigation?
[00:10:18] Maya Patel: for Hosted customers, raw logs are retained briefly but we can provide exports under legal/contractual process; for Dedicated/Private we can make raw logs available per agreement and in BYOK flows we can lock access to those buckets.
[00:10:34] Tom Becker: do you store IP addresses for GDPR? we need to know retention and legal basis.
[00:10:39] Connor Li: we store IPs for security reasons; retention is configurable and can be minimized. we recommend discussing lawful basis with your privacy team. IPs can be hashed in exports if you prefer.
[00:10:54] [00:10:54] Lena Ortiz: want to confirm export formats — NDJSON, Avro, Parquet?
[00:10:59] Connor Li: NDJSON is default; we support Parquet for BigQuery ingestion and Avro on request.
[00:11:09] Maya Patel: time check — you had asked about proof-of-integrity and signed manifests. we'll demo that in the export test.
[00:11:16] Aisha Rahman: excellent. Any blockers for us to start a pilot?
[00:11:20] Maya Patel: no blockers — we'll need the export endpoint (S3 or Kafka) and confirmation on KMS model. also an NDA for SOC2 docs.
[00:11:29] Tom Becker: let's agree next steps: we provide endpoints and retention targets; Red wood provides SOC2 and demo artifacts.
[00:11:35] [00:11:35] Connor Li: i'll prepare a small demo script: 1) generate a few audit events 2) show redaction and deterministic hashing 3) push to S3 and show signed manifest.
[00:11:47] Samir Khan: one thing — can you include a mapping of event types to compliance controls? that's super helpful for auditors.
[00:11:53] Maya Patel: yes, we'll add a control mapping doc.
[00:11:59] [00:11:59] Lena Ortiz: ok thanks everyone, this was good.
[00:12:02] Maya Patel: thanks all — we'll follow up with artifacts and a calendar invite for the export test.
[00:12:08] [End of meeting — 62 minutes recorded according to meeting header]
